newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says British Telecom covered by leased lines directive.
newsitem.headline: Court says British Telecom covered by leased lines directive.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday that British Telecommunications (BT) must be regarded as a "telecommunications organisation", subject to EU rules on open networks and leased lines.

BT argued it should not be subject to the leased lines directive, telling the court it enjoyed no special or exclusive rights within the meaning of the EU's framework Open Network Provision directive.

The court disagreed, saying that both BT and its rival, Mercury Communications, had been given the sole right to operate international links. It said that was "sufficient to constitute the grant for their benefit of exclusive or special rights in respect of public telecommunications networks...."

The court acknowledged that BT and Mercury, which supported the court challenge, were obliged to accept other operators on their networks, but said those constraints were not enough to deprive them of the advantage they enjoy.
"Telecommunications - Directive on open netowrk provisions - Special or exclusive rights - Directive on leased lines - Provision of a minimum set of leased lines"
Reference from the High Court of Justice (Queen's Bench Division) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings before that court between
Secretary of State for Trade and Industry

on the interpretation of Council directive 90/387/EEC of 28 June 1990 on the establishment of the internal market for telecommunciations services through the implemenation of open network provision (OJ 1990 L 192, p. 1) and on the interpretation and validity of Council directive 92/44/EEC of 5 June 1992 on the application of open network provision to leased lines (OJ 1992 L 1654, p. 27)

1. Council directive 92/44/EEC of 5 June 1992 on the application of open network provision to leased lines aplies to "telecommunications organizations" within the meaning of article 2(1) of Council directive 90/387/EEC of 28 June 1990 on the establishment of the internal market for telecommunciations services through the implementation of open network provision. Inter alia, the two undertakings to which a member state has reserved, otherwise than according to objective, proportional and non-discriminatory critera, the operation of international and in particular intra-Community telecommunciations lines and likewise the undertaking to which a member state has reserved, on the same terms, the operation of a public telecommunications network in part of its territory constitute "telecommunications organizations" within the meaning of that provision. A member state is entitled to impose the obligations laid down in article 7 of directive 92/44 on only some "telecommunications organisations", since the imposition of those obligations is sufficient to make available to users throughout the national territory a minimum number of leased lines complying with the specifications laid down by that directive. In particular, a member state is entitled to impose the obligations laid down in that provision on only those "telecommunications organisations" which are the principal operators of telecommunications lines in each of the geographical areas comprising its territory.
2. Examination of the questions referred for a preliminary ruling has disclosed no factor capable of affecting the validity of directive 92/44.
